summary: Steel lookout on the Northern Cheyenne Reservation near Lame Deer, Montana, dated 1930 and last reported standing in 2016; registered with the NHLR in 2022.

facts.status_note: Last reported standing in 2016 by the NHLR and firelookout.com; no newer report found.

access.note: On the Northern Cheyenne Reservation and reached through a wire gate; the sources give no public visiting rules.

visit.trail_note: From Lame Deer, drive east on State Highway 8 about 4.7 miles to a forest road, then follow a bulldozed grade past a wire gate to the tower.

facts.agency: Northern Cheyenne Agency - Bureau of Indian Affairs

events.note: NHLR gives 1930; firelookout.com dates the steel tower to the 1930s
Last reported standing: the NHLR says still standing as of 2016, and firelookout.com says Still there 2016

evidence.supports: steel tower, still standing as of 2016
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s, this steel tower was still standing as of 2016.

evidence.supports: location on the Northern Cheyenne Tribe land in Rosebud County
administered by the Northern Cheyenne Agency of the Bureau of Indian Affairs

evidence.quote: Badger Peak Rosebud 45.64271 -106.54832 Tower Standing NHLR US 1530, MT 93

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR gives 1930, while firelookout.com says 1930s. The 1930 date is consistent with the 1930s, so the record uses 1930 with the range noted.
The FFLOS standing list shows the tower as standing, but the NHLR's own wording is 'still standing as of 2016'. Standing is kept, with the 2016 date in the status note.
The NHLR gives 4,404 ft (1,342 m) and firelookout.com gives 4422 ft. The register figure is the one in the record.

notes_for_editor: Only four sources, one of them an undated station description (the source of the staffing and access route). No notable fires, builder, or reason for construction found in the sources. The 'access' level was changed from 'restricted' to 'unknown': that was an inference from the reservation location and the wire gate, and the sources give no visiting rules. The contact-the-tribe advice had no source and was removed from the story. The brief's claim that firelookout.com is missing from its own standing map was not verified. One WebSearch found no new Badger-specific sources.
